blocks.prompt: 24 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\sin x + \sin 3x + \sin 5x + \sin 7x = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Chaar sines hain jin ke angles ek pattern mein hain: \(x, 3x, 5x, 7x\).
Find kya karna hai? \([0, 2\pi]\) mein solutions aur general solution.
Rule: sum-to-product formulas, pehle sines ke liye aur phir cosines ke liye.
Kaunsi terms jorein? Bahar wali do (\(x\) aur \(7x\)) aur andar wali do (\(3x\) aur \(5x\)); dono joron ki average \(4x\) hai, is liye \(\sin 4x\) common niklega.
Plan: teen factors ka product banana aur har factor ko zero rakh kar dekhna ke kaun se jawab naye hain aur kaun se pehle se maujood.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin x + \sin 3x + \sin 5x + \sin 7x = 0\).
Maloom karna: \([0, 2\pi]\) mein solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: \(\sin C + \sin D = 2\sin\frac{C+D}{2}\cos\frac{C-D}{2}\) ko \((\sin 7x + \sin x)\) aur \((\sin 5x + \sin 3x)\) par lagayenge, phir \(\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\frac{C+D}{2}\cos\frac{C-D}{2}\).

Terms ke jore banayein
\[\sin 7x + \sin x = 2\sin 4x\cos 3x\]
\[\sin 5x + \sin 3x = 2\sin 4x\cos x\]
Kyun: pehle jore mein aadha jama \(\frac{8x}{2} = 4x\) aur aadha farq \(\frac{6x}{2} = 3x\); doosre mein aadha jama \(\frac{8x}{2} = 4x\) aur aadha farq \(\frac{2x}{2} = x\). Dono mein \(\sin 4x\) aa gaya, yahi hum chahte the.

\(2\sin 4x\) common nikalein
\[2\sin 4x(\cos 3x + \cos x) = 0\]
\[2\sin 4x \cdot 2\cos 2x\cos x = 0\]
\[4\sin 4x\cos 2x\cos x = 0\]
Kyun: bracket mein cosines ka jama hai; \(\cos 3x + \cos x = 2\cos\frac{4x}{2}\cos\frac{2x}{2} = 2\cos 2x\cos x\). Ab poori left side teen factors ka product hai.

Har factor hal karein
\[\sin 4x = 0:\ x = \tfrac{n\pi}{4}\]
\[\cos 2x = 0:\ 2x = \tfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\]
\[x = \tfrac{\pi}{4} + \tfrac{n\pi}{2}\]
\[\cos x = 0:\ x = \tfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\]
Kyun: sine \(\pi\) ke multiples par zero hota hai; cosine \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) par zero hota hai, jo \(\pi\) ke faasle par hain, is liye \(\frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\).
Yaad rakhiye: product mein jitne factors hon, utne cases bante hain; yahan teen factors, to teen cases.

Aakhri do families koi naya jawab nahi deteen
\[\tfrac{\pi}{4}, \tfrac{3\pi}{4}, \tfrac{5\pi}{4}, \ldots \text{ aur } \tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{3\pi}{2}, \ldots\]
Kyun: yeh sab \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ke multiples hain, jo \(x = \frac{n\pi}{4}\) mein pehle se shamil hain. Asal wajah: \(\sin 4x = 2\sin 2x\cos 2x = 4\sin x\cos x\cos 2x\), to jab \(\cos 2x = 0\) ya \(\cos x = 0\) ho, \(\sin 4x\) khud bhi zero hota hai.
Dhyan dein: teeno families alag alag likh dena ghalat nahi, magar ek hi value ko do teen dafa ginna ghalat hai.

\([0, 2\pi]\) mein values (\(n = 0, \ldots, 8\))
\[0, \tfrac{\pi}{4}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{3\pi}{4}, \pi, \tfrac{5\pi}{4}, \tfrac{3\pi}{2}, \tfrac{7\pi}{4}, 2\pi\]
Kyun: har qadam \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ka hai; \(n = 8\) par theek \(2\pi\), yani 9 values.
To aakhir mein jawab bohat saaf aaya: \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) ke saare multiples.

Tasdeeq: \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\)
\[\sin\tfrac{\pi}{4} + \sin\tfrac{3\pi}{4} + \sin\tfrac{5\pi}{4} + \sin\tfrac{7\pi}{4}\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1 + 1 - 1 - 1) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: yeh chaar angles chaaron quadrants mein hain; sine pehle do mein positive aur aakhri do mein negative hai, sab ki size \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), to jama zero.
